The company announced this strategic leadership move today, highlighting Charlesworth’s role in overseeing the firm's technological advancements. This appointment marks a significant addition to the executive team as the organization continues to develop its digital trading infrastructure for global clients.
content_ta: நிறுவன ரீதியான மூலதனச் சந்தைகளுக்கான இணைய வர்த்தக தீர்வுகளில் முன்னணியில் உள்ள Caplin Systems, தனது புதிய தலைமை தொழில்நுட்ப அதிகாரியாக (CTO) Steve Charlesworth-ஐ நியமித்துள்ளது. நிறுவனத்தின் தொழில்நுட்ப மேம்பாடுகளை வழிநடத்தும் பொறுப்பை அவர் ஏற்றுக்கொள்வார் என்று இன்று அறிவிக்கப்பட்டுள்ளது. உலகளாவிய வாடிக்கையாளர்களுக்கான டிஜிட்டல் வர்த்தக உள்கட்டமைப்பை உருவாக்குவதில் ஈடுபட்டுள்ள இந்த நிறுவனத்தின் நிர்வாகக் குழுவில், இந்த நியமனம் ஒரு முக்கிய மைல்கல்லாகக் கருதப்படுகிறது.

title: Bitget launches token stock transfer service
summary: Bitget, the world's largest Universal Exchange (UEX), has launched rToken Stock Transfer, enabling users to transfer eligible US-listed stocks and ETFs from traditional brokerage accounts into Bitget as tokenized stocks (rTokens).
content: Cryptocurrency exchange Bitget has launched the rToken Stock Transfer service. This new offering allows users to transfer eligible US-listed stocks and ETFs from traditional brokerage accounts directly into the Bitget platform, converting them into tokenized stocks known as rTokens.
content_ta: கிரிப்டோகரன்சி எக்ஸ்சேஞ்ச் ஆன Bitget, rToken Stock Transfer சேவையைத் தொடங்கியுள்ளது. இந்த புதிய சேவையின் மூலம் பயனர்கள் தங்களது பாரம்பரிய புரோக்கரேஜ் கணக்குகளில் உள்ள தகுதியான US-listed பங்குகள் மற்றும் ETF-களை நேரடியாக Bitget தளத்திற்கு மாற்றிக்கொள்ள முடியும், அவை rTokens எனப்படும் டோக்கன் செய்யப்பட்ட பங்குகளாக மாற்றப்படும்.

title: UK fintech Capsafa launches financial life organiser
summary: UK fintech startup Capsafa has launched a free financial life organiser to help households keep track of their accounts, documents and renewal dates.
content: UK fintech startup Capsafa has officially launched a free financial life organiser tool. The new platform is designed to help households easily keep track of their various accounts, important documents, and upcoming renewal dates all in one place.
content_ta: UK-வைச் சேர்ந்த fintech நிறுவனமான Capsafa, households தங்களின் accounts, documents மற்றும் renewal dates-ஐ எளிதாக நிர்வகிக்க உதவும் ஒரு புதிய free financial life organiser-ஐ அறிமுகப்படுத்தியுள்ளது.

title: Mintos launches commission-free stock trading
summary: Mintos, a European multi-asset investment platform, is launching commission-free stock investing.
content: Mintos, a European multi-asset investment platform, has officially launched a new commission-free stock trading service. This expansion aims to provide investors with broader access to financial markets by removing transaction fees. The platform, known for its diverse range of investment opportunities, is integrating this feature to enhance its user experience and compete within the European investment landscape, allowing users to build their portfolios more cost-effectively.
content_ta: ஐரோப்பாவைச் சேர்ந்த மல்டி-அசெட் முதலீட்டு தளமான Mintos, கமிஷன் கட்டணம் இல்லாத பங்குகளை வர்த்தகம் செய்யும் புதிய சேவையைத் தொடங்கியுள்ளது. பரிவர்த்தனை கட்டணங்களை நீக்குவதன் மூலம், முதலீட்டாளர்கள் நிதிச் சந்தைகளை எளிதாக அணுகுவதை இந்த விரிவாக்கம் நோக்கமாகக் கொண்டுள்ளது. ஏற்கனவே பல்வேறு முதலீட்டு வாய்ப்புகளை வழங்கி வரும் Mintos தளம், தனது பயனர் அனுபவத்தை மேம்படுத்தவும், ஐரோப்பிய சந்தையில் போட்டியிடவும் இந்த புதிய வசதியை அறிமுகப்படுத்தியுள்ளது. இதன் மூலம் பயனர்கள் குறைந்த செலவில் தங்கள் முதலீட்டு இலாகாவை உருவாக்க முடியும்.

title: Plus500 agrees to acquire Hedge Global Markets
summary: Plus500, a global multi-asset fintech group operating proprietary technology-based trading platforms, is pleased to announce that it has conditionally agreed to acquire Hedge Capital Markets Inc., together with its subsidiaries (“Hedge”), including a US broker-dealer registered with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC”) and a member of the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (“FINRA”) (the “Acquisition”).
content: Global fintech group Plus500 has announced a conditional agreement to acquire Hedge Capital Markets Inc. This acquisition includes the company’s subsidiaries, featuring a US-based broker-dealer that is registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission and is a member of the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority. The move marks a significant expansion for Plus500 as it seeks to strengthen its technological trading capabilities and footprint within the United States regulatory environment.
content_ta: உலகளாவிய நிதி தொழில்நுட்ப நிறுவனமான Plus500, Hedge Capital Markets Inc. நிறுவனத்தை கையகப்படுத்துவதற்கான நிபந்தனையுடன் கூடிய ஒப்பந்தத்தை அறிவித்துள்ளது. இந்த கையகப்படுத்தலில், அமெரிக்காவின் Securities and Exchange Commission மற்றும் Financial Industry Regulatory Authority ஆகியவற்றில் பதிவுசெய்யப்பட்ட தரகர் நிறுவனமும் அடங்கும். அமெரிக்க சந்தையில் தனது வர்த்தக தொழில்நுட்ப திறன்களையும் தடத்தையும் விரிவுபடுத்துவதை நோக்கமாகக் கொண்டு Plus500 இந்த நடவடிக்கையை மேற்கொண்டுள்ளது.

title: Rain launches stablecoin wallet
summary: Rain, the global stablecoin payments platform, today announced Rain wallets, embedded stablecoin wallets that partners can offer their users inside their own apps, with the ability to earn on balances to follow by end of year.
content: Global stablecoin payments platform Rain has officially launched Rain wallets. This new embedded service enables partners to integrate stablecoin wallet functionality directly into their own applications. Rain plans to further expand this offering by the end of the year, providing users with the capability to earn yields on their stablecoin balances.
content_ta: உலகளாவிய ஸ்டேபிள்காயின் பணப்பரிமாற்ற தளமான Rain, தற்போது Rain wallets என்ற புதிய சேவையை அறிமுகப்படுத்தியுள்ளது. இந்த வசதியின் மூலம், நிறுவனங்கள் தங்கள் சொந்த செயலிகளிலேயே ஸ்டேபிள்காயின் வாலட்களை ஒருங்கிணைக்க முடியும். மேலும், இந்த ஆண்டு இறுதிக்குள் பயனர்கள் தங்கள் வாலட் இருப்புகளுக்கு வட்டி ஈட்டும் வசதியையும் வழங்க Rain திட்டமிட்டுள்ளது.

title: ExpenseIn and Tax Desk join forces for expense management
summary: ExpenseIn, the specialist expense management platform, has established a new partnership with Tax Desk, expanding the support available to businesses looking to simplify, automate and gain greater control over employee expense processes and claims.
content: Expense management platform ExpenseIn has entered into a strategic partnership with Tax Desk. This collaboration aims to enhance the support offered to businesses, helping them streamline and automate their internal employee expense processes. By joining forces, the two companies provide organizations with improved control and efficiency regarding expense claims, enabling a more integrated approach to managing corporate financial operations.
content_ta: Expense management தளமான ExpenseIn, Tax Desk நிறுவனத்துடன் புதிய கூட்டாண்மையை ஏற்படுத்தியுள்ளது. இந்த கூட்டணியின் மூலம், நிறுவனங்கள் தங்கள் ஊழியர்களின் செலவு மேலாண்மை மற்றும் கோரிக்கைகளை எளிதாக்கவும், தானியக்கமாக்கவும் தேவையான கூடுதல் ஆதரவை வழங்க திட்டமிட்டுள்ளன. இந்த இணைப்பின் வாயிலாக, வணிகங்கள் தங்கள் நிதி செயல்பாடுகளை சிறப்பாகவும், துல்லியமாகவும் கண்காணிக்க வழிவகை செய்யப்பட்டுள்ளது.

title: HID appointed to FIDO board
summary: HID, a worldwide leader in trusted identity solutions, has joined the FIDO Alliance Board of Directors to help accelerate the shift to passwordless authentication across the enterprise.
content: HID, a global leader in trusted identity solutions, has officially joined the FIDO Alliance Board of Directors. This strategic move aims to accelerate the industry-wide transition toward passwordless authentication for enterprises. By joining the board, HID will collaborate with other major organizations to advance secure digital identity standards and promote the adoption of FIDO protocols, helping businesses improve security and user experience by reducing reliance on traditional passwords.
content_ta: நம்பகமான அடையாள தீர்வுகளில் உலகளாவிய முன்னணியில் இருக்கும் HID, FIDO Alliance-ன் இயக்குநர்கள் குழுவில் இணைந்துள்ளது. நிறுவனங்கள் கடவுச்சொல் இல்லா (passwordless) அங்கீகார முறைக்கு மாறுவதை ஊக்குவிப்பதே இந்த கூட்டணியின் முக்கிய நோக்கமாகும். இந்த இணைப்பின் மூலம், பாதுகாப்பான டிஜிட்டல் அடையாள தரநிலைகளை மேம்படுத்தவும், FIDO நெறிமுறைகளை உலகம் முழுவதும் கொண்டு செல்லவும் HID மற்ற முன்னணி நிறுவனங்களுடன் இணைந்து செயல்படும். இதன் மூலம் நிறுவனங்களின் பாதுகாப்பு மற்றும் பயனர் அனுபவத்தை மேம்படுத்த முடியும்.

title: B2Prime extends liquidity management tool
summary: B2PRIME Group, a global financial services provider for institutional and professional clients, has announced a material expansion of its institutional liquidity architecture.
content: B2PRIME Group, a global financial services provider, has announced a significant expansion of its institutional liquidity management tools. This development aims to enhance the company's existing liquidity architecture, catering specifically to the needs of professional and institutional clients. By extending these capabilities, B2PRIME continues to strengthen its infrastructure, focusing on improving service delivery and operational efficiency for its diverse global client base within the financial markets.
content_ta: உலகளாவிய நிதிச் சேவை நிறுவனமான B2PRIME Group, தனது நிறுவன அளவிலான பணப்புழக்க மேலாண்மை (liquidity management) கருவிகளை விரிவுபடுத்துவதாக அறிவித்துள்ளது. இந்த நடவடிக்கை, தொழில்முறை மற்றும் நிறுவன வாடிக்கையாளர்களின் தேவைகளைப் பூர்த்தி செய்யும் வகையில் அதன் ஏற்கனவே உள்ள பணப்புழக்க கட்டமைப்பை மேம்படுத்துவதை நோக்கமாகக் கொண்டுள்ளது. இந்த கூடுதல் வசதிகள் மூலம், நிதிச் சந்தைகளில் தனது வாடிக்கையாளர்களுக்குச் சிறந்த சேவைகளை வழங்குவதையும், செயல்பாட்டுத் திறனை அதிகரிப்பதையும் B2PRIME நோக்கமாகக் கொண்டுள்ளது.

title: Culture Shifts: Why the Industry Is Already Moving Beyond T+1
summary: At Sibos 2026, Smartstream’s Nick Smith talks about how banks are progressing at different speeds towards real-time payments, intraday liquidity management and post-trade automation, largely because of differences in culture, priorities, data quality and legacy technology.
content: At Sibos 2026, industry experts noted that the move toward real-time payments and post-trade automation is accelerating beyond the T+1 transition. Smartstream’s Nick Smith highlighted that banks are advancing at varying speeds due to disparities in internal culture, data infrastructure, and legacy technology. These factors dictate how financial institutions prioritize intraday liquidity management and operational efficiency in a rapidly evolving global market landscape.
content_ta: Sibos 2026 மாநாட்டில், T+1 பரிவர்த்தனை முறையைத் தாண்டி நிகழ்நேர பணப்பரிமாற்றம் மற்றும் வர்த்தகத்திற்குப் பிந்தைய பணிகளைத் தானியங்குபடுத்தும் முயற்சியில் வங்கிகள் ஈடுபட்டுள்ளதாகத் தெரிவிக்கப்பட்டுள்ளது. Smartstream நிறுவனத்தின் Nick Smith குறிப்பிடுகையில், வங்கிகளின் நிறுவன கலாச்சாரம், தரவு மேலாண்மை மற்றும் பழைய தொழில்நுட்பக் கட்டமைப்புகளில் உள்ள வேறுபாடுகளே, இந்த மாற்றத்திற்கான வேகத்தைத் தீர்மானிக்கின்றன என்றார். நிறுவனங்கள் தங்கள் பணப்புழக்க மேலாண்மை மற்றும் செயல்பாட்டுத் திறனை மேம்படுத்த இத்தகைய சவால்களை எதிர்கொண்டு வருகின்றன.

title: The banking app doesn't earn the revenue. It decides who keeps it
summary: Author: A finextra community member
content: A Finextra community member argues that modern banking applications are shifting from simple revenue-generating tools to strategic gatekeepers of wealth. Rather than acting merely as transaction processors, these apps are increasingly designed to manage and control capital flow. This evolution reflects a broader trend where the primary value of banking software lies in the authority to determine how assets are held, allocated, and preserved within the digital ecosystem.
content_ta: நவீன வங்கி செயலிகள் வருமானம் ஈட்டும் கருவிகளாக மட்டுமல்லாமல், செல்வத்தை நிர்வகிக்கும் முக்கிய அதிகார மையங்களாக மாறிவருவதாக Finextra சமூக உறுப்பினர் ஒருவர் சுட்டிக்காட்டியுள்ளார். பணப் பரிவர்த்தனைகளை மேற்கொள்வதை விட, சொத்துக்களின் இருப்பு மற்றும் மேலாண்மையை தீர்மானிப்பதிலேயே இந்த செயலிகளின் உண்மையான மதிப்பு அடங்கியுள்ளது. டிஜிட்டல் சூழலில் நிதி எங்கு சேமிக்கப்பட வேண்டும் மற்றும் எவ்வாறு பயன்படுத்தப்பட வேண்டும் என்பதை முடிவு செய்யும் முக்கிய சக்தியாக வங்கி மென்பொருள்கள் பரிணமித்து வருகின்றன.

title: AI Flywheel Series:Why Learning and Development Must Become an Engine of Organisational Intelligence
summary: Author: A finextra community member
content: In the latest installment of the AI Flywheel series, the discussion highlights how Learning and Development (L&D) functions are evolving. Rather than being simple training departments, they are repositioning themselves as engines for organizational intelligence. By integrating artificial intelligence, firms can cultivate a workforce that is more adaptive, data-driven, and prepared for future industry shifts. This transition is essential for maintaining a competitive edge in an increasingly automated global business environment.
content_ta: AI Flywheel தொடரின் சமீபத்திய பகுதியில், Learning and Development (L&D) துறைகள் எவ்வாறு பரிணமிக்க வேண்டும் என்பது குறித்து விவாதிக்கப்பட்டுள்ளது. வெறும் பயிற்சி பிரிவுகளாக இல்லாமல், நிறுவனத்தின் அறிவுசார் திறனை வளர்க்கும் இயந்திரங்களாக இவை செயல்பட வேண்டும். செயற்கை நுண்ணறிவை இணைப்பதன் மூலம், ஊழியர்களைத் தரவு சார்ந்த முடிவுகளை எடுக்கவும், எதிர்கால மாற்றங்களுக்குத் தயாராகவும் நிறுவனங்கள் மாற்ற முடியும். மாறிவரும் நவீன வணிக சூழலில் போட்டித்தன்மையுடன் இருக்க இந்த மாற்றம் மிகவும் அவசியமானது.

title: Real-Time Fiscal Control: Inside the Machine Learning Revolution in Project Budgeting Analytics
summary: Author: A finextra community member
content: Machine learning is fundamentally changing how organizations manage project budgets. By enabling real-time fiscal control, these advanced analytical tools allow teams to track expenditures instantly and predict potential overruns before they impact financial health. As explored by a Finextra community member, this technological shift moves project management away from reactive manual reporting toward a more proactive, data-driven strategy, ultimately enhancing corporate transparency and operational efficiency across complex business projects.
content_ta: Machine learning தொழில்நுட்பம் நிறுவனங்களின் திட்ட வரவு செலவுத் திட்டத்தை நிர்வகிக்கும் முறையை மாற்றியமைக்கிறது. நிகழ்நேர நிதி கட்டுப்பாட்டை செயல்படுத்துவதன் மூலம், இத்தகைய மேம்பட்ட பகுப்பாய்வு கருவிகள் செலவுகளை உடனுக்குடன் கண்காணிக்கவும், திட்டத்தின் நிதி நிலையைப் பாதிக்கும் முன்பே கூடுதல் செலவுகளைக் கண்டறியவும் உதவுகின்றன. Finextra சமூக உறுப்பினர் குறிப்பிடுவது போல, இந்த தொழில்நுட்ப மாற்றம் திட்ட மேலாண்மையை கையேடு அறிக்கையிடலில் இருந்து மாறி, தரவு சார்ந்த மூலோபாயத்திற்கு கொண்டு செல்கிறது. இது பெருநிறுவன வெளிப்படைத்தன்மையையும் செயல்பாட்டுத் திறனையும் மேம்படுத்துகிறது.

title: Lumepay’s Luc Varejes on fixing the plumbing of African cross-border payments, starting in Kenya
summary:
Lumepay Obtains Regulatory Clearance to Launch Multi-Rail Cross-Border Payment Infrastructure in Kenya
The post Lumepay’s Luc Varejes on fixing the plumbing of African cross-border payments, starting in Kenya appeared first on The Fintech Times.
content: Lumepay has received regulatory approval to introduce its multi-rail cross-border payment infrastructure in Kenya. Led by Luc Varejes, the company aims to modernize the underlying plumbing of African financial transactions to improve efficiency. This launch marks a significant step for Lumepay in expanding its regional payment solutions, focusing on simplifying and streamlining how money moves across borders within the African market.
content_ta: Lumepay நிறுவனம் கென்யாவில் தனது பன்முக எல்லை தாண்டிய கட்டண உள்கட்டமைப்பை அறிமுகப்படுத்த ஒழுங்குமுறை அனுமதியைப் பெற்றுள்ளது. Luc Varejes தலைமையிலான இந்நிறுவனம், ஆப்பிரிக்க நிதிப் பரிவர்த்தனைகளின் அடிப்படை கட்டமைப்பை நவீனப்படுத்தி செயல்திறனை மேம்படுத்த இலக்கு வைத்துள்ளது. ஆப்பிரிக்க சந்தையில் எல்லை தாண்டிய பணப் பரிமாற்றங்களை எளிதாக்குவதையும் நெறிப்படுத்துவதையும் நோக்கமாகக் கொண்டு, Lumepay தனது பிராந்திய பணப்பரிமாற்ற சேவைகளை விரிவுபடுத்த இந்த முயற்சி ஒரு முக்கிய மைல்கல்லாகும்.

content_ta: Money20/20 USA, Las Vegas-ல் நடைபெறவுள்ள 2026-ம் ஆண்டிற்கான தனது திட்டங்களை அறிவித்துள்ளது. இந்த மாநாட்டில் செயற்கை நுண்ணறிவு (AI) மாற்றம், எல்லைகளைக் கடந்த நிதி உள்கட்டமைப்பு மற்றும் புதிய ஒழுங்குமுறை விதிகள் ஆகியவை முக்கிய விவாதப் பொருளாக இருக்கும். உலகளாவிய நிதிச் சேவைகளின் எதிர்காலத்தை வடிவமைக்கும் தலைவர்கள் இந்த நிகழ்வில் ஒன்றிணைந்து, இத்துறையின் வளர்ச்சிக்கான முக்கிய உத்திகள் குறித்து விவாதிக்க உள்ளனர்.

title: Why Salient bet everything on auto lending and never looked back
summary:
Most AI startups chase breadth. They build a capable, general-purpose product and sell it across as many industries as are willing to buy it. Ari Malik, CEO of Salient, took the opposite approach. He picked one vertical, auto lending, and went deep enough that he eventually moved his company’s headquarters to Los Angeles to be …

content: Unlike most AI startups that prioritize broad, general-purpose products, Salient chose to specialize in a single niche. CEO Ari Malik focused the company's efforts entirely on auto lending. This strategy involved deepening their expertise in that specific industry, even leading to a relocation of their headquarters to Los Angeles to better serve the sector and cement their vertical-focused business model.
content_ta: பெரும்பாலான AI ஸ்டார்ட்அப்கள் பொதுவான தயாரிப்புகளை உருவாக்குவதில் கவனம் செலுத்தும் வேளையில், Salient நிறுவனம் ஒரு குறிப்பிட்ட துறையை மட்டும் தேர்ந்தெடுத்துச் செயல்படுகிறது. CEO Ari Malik, ஆட்டோ லெண்டிங் (auto lending) துறையில் மட்டும் முழு கவனம் செலுத்தினார். இந்தச் சிறப்பு அணுகுமுறைக்காக, அந்தத் துறையில் தங்கள் நிபுணத்துவத்தை மேம்படுத்திக்கொள்ள Salient நிறுவனம் தனது தலைமையகத்தை Los Angeles-க்கு மாற்றியது.

content: Valley National Bank’s planned acquisition of Bluevine raises questions regarding the integration of fintech companies into traditional banking structures. The acquisition, expected to finalize in 2027, serves as a test case for whether banks can successfully incorporate fintech innovation without compromising the unique operational models that drive their effectiveness.
content_ta: Valley National Bank, Bluevine-ஐ கையகப்படுத்தத் திட்டமிட்டுள்ளது. இந்த ஒப்பந்தம், வங்கித் துறையில் fintech நிறுவனங்கள் இணையும்போது, அவற்றின் தயாரிப்பு மேம்பாடு மற்றும் தொழில்நுட்பக் குழுக்களின் செயல்பாடுகள் எவ்வாறு அமையும் என்ற கேள்வியை எழுப்பியுள்ளது. 2027-ஆம் ஆண்டில் நிறைவடையும் என எதிர்பார்க்கப்படும் இந்த கையகப்படுத்தல், ஒரு வங்கி தனது பாரம்பரிய கட்டமைப்பிற்குள் fintech நிறுவனத்தின் தனித்துவமான செயல்பாட்டு முறையை எவ்வாறு பாதுகாக்கிறது என்பதற்கான முக்கிய உதாரணமாக அமையும்.

content_ta: UK-ன் Financial Conduct Authority மற்றும் National Crime Agency ஆகிய அமைப்புகள், உள்நுழைவு வர்த்தகம் (insider trading) தொடர்பான சந்தேகத்தின் பேரில் கூட்டாக இணைந்து கைது நடவடிக்கைகளை மேற்கொண்டுள்ளன. இந்த நடவடிக்கையின் ஒரு பகுதியாக, ஐந்து வீடுகளில் சோதனை நடத்தப்பட்டு மூன்று நபர்கள் கைது செய்யப்பட்டுள்ளனர். விசாரணையின் ஒரு கட்டமாக, பல மின்னணு சாதனங்களை அதிகாரிகள் கைப்பற்றியுள்ளனர். நிதிச் சந்தையில் நடைபெறும் முறைகேடுகளைத் தடுக்க, UK-ன் இந்த இரு அமைப்புகளும் இணைந்து செயல்படுவது முக்கியமாகக் கருதப்படுகிறது.

title: JPMorgan CEO Dimon warns customers of ‘liability transfer’ with AI

content: JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon has issued a warning regarding the integration of artificial intelligence in banking. As tools like Meta’s Muse raise concerns about automated deposit movements, Dimon highlighted that customers utilizing AI agents must be aware of potential liability transfer risks. The comments underscore growing industry caution over how AI-driven services might impact consumer financial security and accountability during bank transactions.

Meta-வின் Muse போன்ற கருவிகள் மூலம் தானியங்கி முறையில் வைப்புத்தொகைகள் மாற்றப்படுவது குறித்த அச்சம் எழுந்துள்ள நிலையில், AI ஏஜெண்டுகளைப் பயன்படுத்தும் வாடிக்கையாளர்கள் தங்களுக்கு ஏற்படக்கூடிய பொறுப்பு மாற்றங்கள் (liability transfer) மற்றும் அபாயங்களை உணர்ந்து செயல்பட வேண்டும் என்று அவர் அறிவுறுத்தியுள்ளார். வங்கிப் பரிவர்த்தனைகளில் AI-ன் தாக்கம் வாடிக்கையாளர்களின் பாதுகாப்பை எவ்வாறு பாதிக்கும் என்பது குறித்த கவலைகள் அதிகரித்து வருகின்றன.

title: From Raw Data to Actionable Insights: The Acuity Advantage
summary:
OneRoyal’s suite of Acuity AI trading tools helps traders make sense of fast-moving markets, turning news and data into insights that support more informed decisions.
Access to market information has never been easier. However, making sense of that information remains one of the most demanding parts of trading. The sheer volume of corporate announcements and geopolitical developments often leaves traders with more information than they can realistically assess.
A single headline can prompt a price move across several markets. It’s understanding why it matters and whether it changes an existing trading view that takes time. By the time a trader has analysed the news and compared the relevant charts, the market may already have moved again.
As AI makes advanced market analysis more accessible, its practical value lies in helping traders bridge this gap between information and action. For both beginners and experienced traders, the challenge is translating a continuous flow of data into something useful for their strategy.
Through its partnership with Acuity Trading, OneRoyal brings this capability into the trading workflow. Its suite of tools, including SignalX, AssetIQ, Action News, Market Scanner, and Daily Intel, helps traders put market developments into context and identify ideas worth exploring.
Making market information useful
Manual research requires traders to piece together information from different sources. They have to find news feeds explaining the latest developments and a chart showing the price response, all while analysing whether the move reflects a broader trend. The lengthy process can leave traders falling behind.
OneRoyal’s Acuity suite uses machine learning to analyse the latest news across thousands of markets in real time, providing context for price movements alongside actionable trade ideas. This gives traders a more focused starting point for their own assessment.
Action News, for example, helps filter the flow of headlines so traders can concentrate on developments relevant to the markets they follow. Around a major economic release, that focus can help them assess the news alongside the price response.
SignalX and AssetIQ bring further perspective through insights into sentiment, trends, price patterns, and key levels. These inputs can help traders examine whether a potential opportunity supports their existing market view or gives them a reason to reconsider it.
Even though an actionable insight provides a basis for evaluation, traders still need to decide for themselves whether an idea fits their objectives and timeframe.
Analysis that fits the strategy
For analytical tools to become useful on a day to day basis, they need to work within a trader’s existing routine. Constantly switching between research sources can interrupt that process, especially when market conditions are changing quickly.
OneRoyal’s suite is designed to integrate into traders’ strategies, making relevant intelligence easier to incorporate into their analysis. Market Scanner supports this process by summarising data across thousands of assets and highlighting strategy-specific trade ideas. Alongside Daily Intel and the wider suite, it gives traders additional resources for keeping their research current.
For a beginner, this can make the research process more approachable by providing specific developments and signals to investigate. An experienced trader can use the same tools to narrow a watchlist or identify a market that warrants closer attention.
Take the example of a trader monitoring an asset ahead of an economic announcement. Relevant news and key price levels can help them prepare scenarios before the release. As new information arrives, they can assess it against that preparation and decide whether their original reasoning is justified.
Supporting a more proactive approach
The ability to process information quickly gives traders more time to consider its implications. Reacting to a headline without understanding its context often leads to poorly considered decisions.
AI cannot remove market uncertainty or guarantee a successful trade. It can, however, make the analytical work more manageable, helping traders evaluate potential opportunities and adjust their views as conditions change.
By integrating Acuity’s analytical capabilities into its offering, OneRoyal supports this more proactive approach to trading. With less time spent gathering and interpreting raw data, traders have more room to assess opportunities against their strategy and make informed decisions.

title: Why Regulation Must Keep Pace with Payment Innovation Ahead of Proposed BoE Innovation
summary:
The Government intends to add innovation to the Bank of England’s remit, alongside its primary responsibility for financial stability. The change covers the payment systems and newer forms of digital money that fall within the Bank's regulatory scope. That is a positive direction. The payments industry moves quickly, but regulation understandably takes time to develop. The challenge is making sure businesses have enough visibility while new rules are being worked through to make sensible decisions about where to invest, what to build and how new technology can be introduced safely.
I would like to see the Bank's new objective encourage an even stronger working relationship between regulators and payment companies as that process develops. HM Treasury's National Payments Vision refers to "significant regulatory congestion" across the current payments landscape, with programmes from government, regulators and industry all moving at once. For payment companies, that means keeping a constant eye on rule changes, often involving different bodies, while still trying to build products and solutions for merchants.
Clarity can influence investment
There is evidence that investors are more willing to back a company when the regulatory position is clearer.
A Bank for International Settlements study looked at companies that went through the Financial Conduct Authority's regulatory sandbox and found a 15 per cent increase in capital raised, while the likelihood of raising funding increased by 50 per cent. The researchers linked some of that effect to lower regulatory costs and fewer information gaps.
HM Treasury's National Payments Vision says regulation should be "clear, predictable and proportionate". Predictable is the word I would focus on.
Payment companies need a decent idea of what they are building towards before too much time and money have been committed. Regulation will evolve as technologies and markets change and businesses should expect that. But there is a significant difference between adapting to a clearly signposted direction and having to rethink a strategy late in the development process.
That predictability becomes even more important when companies are investing in infrastructure that needs to work across multiple merchants, markets and regulatory requirements.
The industry needs a say before a proposal becomes a rule
Under its new secondary objective, the Bank must report to Parliament each year on what it has done to support innovation. That annual report could become a useful measure of how the relationship between regulation and industry is working in practice. It should show not just how many consultations or roundtables have taken place, but where industry feedback has materially influenced the development of policy. I would want to see where a proposal moved, or remained unchanged, because businesses raised an operational, commercial or technical consequence that needed to be considered.
Consultation should not mean industry gets everything it asks for. Regulators have wider responsibilities, particularly around financial stability and consumer protection. But businesses need the opportunity to explain how proposals will operate once they move from a policy document into a live payment environment. That dialogue is particularly important when the technology itself is evolving quickly.
New technology still has to earn its place
Merchants and acquirers are making decisions off the back of all this too, even if they never read a Bank of England consultation themselves. In a busy retail store, payment data can already feed into fraud checks or financial reconciliation. At a high-end hotel, the transaction may be large, but the customer still expects it to go through quickly and discreetly. Any new payment method or technology has to fit into everything already happening around those transactions.
Payments used to be judged primarily on whether the transaction went through. That is still fundamental, but the data surrounding a payment has become almost as valuable as processing the transaction itself. It can show a business where customers are dropping out partway through a purchase, where revenue may be going missing, or where an emerging risk deserves closer attention.
A merchant still has to decide whether changing its payment setup is worth the cost and disruption. If new technology fixes a problem the business already has, the case is relatively easy to understand. "It's new" is a much harder sell. That is especially true when new technology has to be introduced across existing payment infrastructure. The customer may only see a new terminal, checkout option or payment method, but behind that can sit changes to integration, data flows, reconciliation and operational processes. The aim is for all of that work to remain largely invisible to the customer.
Late changes to the rules can make implementation harder. By then, work may already be under way and money committed.
Clear rules also mean knowing who is responsible
As more information moves into the payment layer, the boundary between the payment provider and the merchant becomes increasingly important. In retail, for example, transaction data can help identify patterns that suggest fraud, payment failure or unusual purchasing behaviour. But technology can only surface the information. The merchant still needs to decide what action to take and remain accountable for that decision.
Payment technology can therefore give a business better information without changing where responsibility ultimately sits.
That boundary needs to remain clear as new payment models develop. A company can build around a demanding rule when it knows where its responsibility starts and stops. Ambiguity becomes much harder to deal with once the technology is already live.
The Bank of England's new innovation objective is therefore most useful if it helps create greater visibility earlier in the process. Innovation needs regulation that businesses can understand, plan around and build against with confidence.
It is a lot easier to build something new when everyone knows where the lines are.

Industry leaders emphasize that clear, predictable regulation is essential for businesses to invest in payment technologies confidently. title: European Businesses Say Outdated Financial Services Are Holding Back Growth
summary:
European business decision makers (‘businesses’) feel they are being treated as second-class customers by financial providers, according to new research.
The findings from CRIF – a global leader in credit and insurance information, analytics and solutions – are published today in Closing the financial services gap for European businesses, the second report in its 2026 Banking on Banks series.
The research finds that four in ten European businesses (41%) say a lack of innovation in financial services is stifling their company’s growth potential, rising to more than half in Ireland (52%). Alongside these growth concerns, almost half of European businesses (45%) said they feel treated as a secondary priority by financial providers, rising to 56% in Ireland and 50% in Italy, with four in ten (43%) saying business financial services receive less innovation than consumer-focused services.
That gap is creating friction, with 57% of businesses saying financial services are faster and simpler for consumers than for companies, 56% reporting more paperwork and manual processes in business banking, and 52% saying it is harder to meet eligibility requirements for business finance than in their personal lives.
As a result, more than half (54%) say they wish they could access business financial services as easily as personal finance services, such as through an app, while two in five (40%) say digital services for businesses are poor compared with what they use personally.
Business banking in the UK: still falling short of the consumer experience
In the UK specifically, progress on bringing business banking in line with consumer standards has been mixed.  The CMA’s retail banking market investigation, launched in 2014, set out specifically to improve banking for SMEs, with CRIF’s research showing there has been progress. Two thirds of UK businesses (66%) say lending decisions have become faster over the past decade, while 52% of UK SMEs say access to finance has improved.
However, CRIF’s research finds that 44% of UK businesses feel it is fintech and alternative lenders that are now more responsive to their business needs compared with traditional banks, against just 16% who disagree. More than a third (36%) of UK businesses feel banks and other financial providers do not understand the needs of businesses like theirs.
Despite improvements to business banking, the gap with consumer services remains. Six in ten (61%) UK businesses say financial services are faster and simpler for consumers, while in the last 12 months one in ten (11%) UK businesses say they have taken out a business loan from an alternative lender.
Sara Costantini, Regional Director for the UK & Ireland at CRIF, said: “Financial services have been transformed for consumers over the past decade, but businesses have not benefited from the same pace of innovation. What is most concerning for the sector, and indeed policymakers, is that so many businesses in Europe now see this directly constraining their growth.
“In the UK specifically, businesses can see the progress made, from faster decisions and better digital tools to improved access to credit, reflecting the maturity of the UK sector. But the gap with consumers persists. Business owners judge their experience against what they get in their personal lives, and by that measure business banking still lags behind.
“Businesses across Europe are clear that they want the same standard of digital financial services for their company as they get in their personal lives. Providers that close this gap will be best placed to retain and attract customers, while crucially supporting growth across the continent.”
The research findings form part of CRIF’s 2026 Banking on Banks report series. The first report, launched in June, looked at the biggest financial pressures currently facing European consumers and businesses.

content: New research from CRIF indicates that many European businesses feel neglected by financial service providers, claiming that a lack of innovation compared to consumer-focused services is hindering their growth. title: UK Venture Funds Raise $6.9bn in Strongest Fundraising Quarter on Record
summary:
UK venture capital firms raised $6.9 billion across 31 new funds in the third quarter of 2026, the strongest fundraising quarter on record and more than four times the quarterly average of the past two years, according to new analysis from HSBC Innovation Banking UK and Dealroom.
The record quarter comes as UK startups and scaleups attracted $6.1 billion in venture capital investment, maintaining the UK’s position as Europe's leading venture market.
Fundraising was driven by established venture managers across several major fund raises. Index Ventures closed three new funds worth a combined $3.5 billion across seed, venture and growth strategies. Highland Europe raised €1.1 billion for its sixth growth fund, and QuantumLight raised $500 million for its second fund, while Crane Venture Partners raised $484 million across four new funds.
Together, the 31 funds closed during the quarter represent a substantial pool of new capital available to back the next generation of startups and scaleups.
Late-stage rounds drive UK venture investment
Late-stage businesses accounted for most of the capital raised during the quarter, attracting $3.5 billion, equivalent to 58% of total UK venture investment.
Major rounds included CityFibre’s $1.2 billion raise, FNZ’s $450 million round and OLIX’s $312 million funding. Breakout-stage companies raised a further $1.9 billion, while early-stage businesses attracted $740 million.
Fintech and health remained among the UK’s most active venture sectors, recording 51 and 62 funding rounds respectively during the quarter.
Semiconductor startups raised $497 million during the quarter, taking total investment in the sector to $1.6 billion in 2026 and already surpassing the previous full-year record of $1.3 billion set in 2025. Almost half of all UK semiconductor funding since 2010 has now been raised in the past two years, underlining the recent acceleration in investment in the sector.
Domestic investors also played a prominent role in UK deal activity, with nine of the ten most active investors in UK funding rounds during Q3 headquartered in the UK. Together, those investors participated in 60 deals during the quarter.
UK maintains European venture leadership
The UK continued to lead Europe for venture capital investment during Q3, attracting 25% of all investment across the continent. Across the first nine months of 2026, UK startups and scaleups have raised $23.3 billion, representing 35% of European venture capital and more than twice the amount attracted by either Germany or France.
Emily Turner, CEO, HSBC Innovation Banking UK, said: “The record level of venture fundraising this quarter is an encouraging signal for the UK innovation ecosystem. Capital raised today gives investors greater firepower to back ambitious businesses through their next stages of growth, and the breadth of new funds being raised shows continued confidence in the opportunities ahead.
“Investment will always fluctuate from quarter to quarter, but the UK continues to have the ingredients that matter: ambitious founders, world-class research and experienced investors with capital to deploy. Maintaining that momentum will be critical to helping more promising companies build and scale from the UK.”

title: Paymentology and Huru Expand Partnership to Launch Jaywan Card in the UAE
summary:
Paymentology, the leading global issuer processor, and Huru, the Emirati-owned financial app licensed by the Central Bank of the UAE, have expanded their longstanding partnership to support the launch of Huru’s card on Jaywan, the UAE’s domestic card scheme.
 Scheduled to launch in Q4 2026, Huru’s Jaywan card will be supported by Paymentology’s processing technology, building on the companies’ existing partnership as Huru broadens the services available to customers across the UAE. 
Huru has grown significantly since launching, with AED 3 billion in annualised salary flows now passing through Huru accounts and more than 24,000 employers using the platform to pay employees. The company is also working with nine exchange houses as it looks to accelerate adoption of the Universal Account, with a target of approximately one million accounts over the coming year.
The Universal Account gives customers an individual IBAN-based account that is linked to them rather than to a specific employer. This means customers can continue using the same account even when their employment changes, reducing the need to repeatedly switch salary arrangements and providing a more consistent way to manage everyday finances.
Through the Huru app, customers can receive their salary, make domestic and international payments, send money overseas, top up mobile phones, set money aside towards savings goals and use their Huru card, with the platform currently available in seven languages.
The addition of Jaywan will further develop Huru’s card proposition while supporting the UAE’s wider move towards a stronger domestic payments ecosystem.
Nauman Hassan, Regional Director MENA at Paymentology, said: “The UAE is building a payments ecosystem that is increasingly shaped by local innovation, digital-first services and greater customer choice. Jaywan is an important part of that evolution, and Huru is well placed to bring those benefits to a broad and growing customer base.
“Our role is to give Huru the processing flexibility and scale it needs to bring new capabilities to market quickly and confidently. Supporting its move onto Jaywan is a natural next step in our partnership, and one that reflects the strength of what we are building together in the UAE.”
Abhimanyu Girotra, Chief Executive Officer of Huru, said: “Receiving a salary is only the starting point of someone’s financial journey. Our focus has always been on what happens next — how people can manage their money, make payments, send money home, save for the future and have greater control over their income.
“Paymentology has been an important partner in helping us build and scale that experience. Bringing Jaywan into the Huru ecosystem is another significant step forward, allowing us to continue evolving the Universal Account while giving our customers access to payment experiences that are increasingly aligned with the UAE’s own financial infrastructure.”
The collaboration reflects the continued development of the UAE payments market, where domestic infrastructure, digital-first financial services and modern processing technology are increasingly coming together to create more locally tailored payment experiences.

title: Visa Receives Approval to Begin Preparations for a Domestic Business in China
summary:
Visa, a global leader in digital payments, today announced that it has received approval of its Application to Prepare from the People’s Bank of China (PBOC), which allows the company to begin formal preparations to establish a domestic bankcard clearing institution in China. This marks an important milestone toward the company serving China’s domestic payments market.
“The approval of our Application to Prepare marks a significant step forward in Visa’s long-standing commitment to China. We greatly appreciate the important role of the leaders of the United States and China in pursuing a constructive and strategically stable relationship between the world’s largest economies,” said Ryan McInerney, Chief Executive Officer of Visa. “For more than 40 years, Visa has been an active contributor to China’s dynamic payments landscape. We look forward to taking the necessary steps in the process, pursuant to the PBOC’s regulations, to begin operating domestically in China.”
China is one of the world’s most advanced and dynamic digital payments markets, supported by a highly innovative ecosystem and continued commitment to further financial sector liberalization. Visa looks forward to bringing its world-class innovation, security and reliability to Chinese consumers and businesses, contributing to the continued development of China’s domestic payments landscape.
Visa will continue its efforts to complete the process and begin domestic bankcard clearing operations in China.

title: From Earth to Orbit, France’s Ecosystem Delivers Agentic Computing at Scale with NVIDIA
summary:
Companies in France are deploying agentic computing across industries spanning space, financial services, the public sector and scientific research, demonstrating how the country’s ecosystem has moved from ambition to application. 
France’s progress sits on deliberate groundwork. 
The AI Action Summit in February 2025 and Choose France Summits in 2025 and 2026 anchored major compute commitments on French soil. What the ecosystem has built since then spans the full stack.

Sovereign AI Infrastructure
France-based companies are expanding agentic infrastructure on NVIDIA technology.

Integrated by Loft Orbital and built in Abu Dhabi by Orbitworks, a joint venture between Loft Orbital and Marlan Space, the satellite is flying NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin edge modules, running Mistral’s models, for real-time Earth observation and autonomous operations in orbit.
Open Models
NVIDIA Nemotron open models are in production across French organizations that require sovereign, trustworthy data. 
LINAGORA and Docaposte have secured the CANUT framework agreement, making Twake.ai, built on NVIDIA Nemotron, the sole referenced sovereign digital workplace for more than 2,500 French public organizations. 
In financial services, SBS is launching a sovereign platform enabling banks to deploy governed generative and agentic services within their own environments, in collaboration with NVIDIA.

Fondation Inria, with NVIDIA’s support, is launching a working group on open source advanced modeling and tool adoption, with findings to come in the spring of next year. 
Agents at Work Across Industries
Across retail, public services, telecommunications and science, the pattern is consistent: open models and NVIDIA infrastructure are driving results in France. 
L’Oréal is integrating NVIDIA ALCHEMI into its research workflows so scientists can explore formulation possibilities in silico and better help guide laboratory research. Combining computational predictions with hands-on experimentation can make the discovery process up to 100x faster than traditional methods and maximize the potential of the group’s proprietary active ingredients.
Mirakl has onboarded more than 70 million products with fine-tuned and open models running on NVIDIA GPUs and inference software, cutting seller catalog onboarding to under two hours.
Photoroom and Vestiaire Collective are demonstrating the measurable business impact of advanced visual modeling on marketplace performance. 
Omi helps brands bring accurate products into AI-generated marketing visuals at scale, combining its approved 3D digital twins with open models optimized on NVIDIA for 4x faster inference.
In Côte-d’Or, ThinkDeep and Akila built a digital-twin agent — powered by NVIDIA Cosmos open world models, Nemotron and Omniverse libraries — managing nearly 5,800 kilometers of roads and buildings, cutting total operating costs by 10% and targeting 30% as deployment progresses. 
Port Sud de France runs goods processing and port security on ThinkDeep’s DeepBrain platform powered by Nemotron and Cosmos. 
Enchanted Tools, a robotics company headquartered in Paris, is deploying social robots to support patients in healthcare settings including pediatric cancer care.
In telecom, Bouygues Telecom and Prisme.ai have launched AI Studio V2, powered by NVIDIA full-stack infrastructure, to offer all of its employees the ability to build their own agents, securely and in a controlled environment
In quantum, Alice & Bob has integrated the NVIDIA NVQLink platform for its superconducting cat qubits, showing how GPUs can make quantum error correction more efficient, including for faster qubit modalities.

By adding Klarna, Ecommpay aims to enhance the checkout experience, improve conversion rates for merchants, and provide shoppers with greater control over their purchases without requiring additional technical work.
content_ta: Ecommpay தனது உலகளாவிய கட்டணத் தளத்தில் Klarna-வை இணைத்துள்ளது. இதன் மூலம் வணிகர்கள் வாடிக்கையாளர்களுக்கு Pay in 3, Pay in 30 days மற்றும் நீண்டகால நிதியுதவி போன்ற நெகிழ்வான கட்டண முறைகளை எளிதாக வழங்க முடியும். ஒரே ஒருங்கிணைப்பு மூலம் இந்த வசதி கிடைப்பதால், வணிகர்களுக்கு கூடுதல் தொழில்நுட்ப வேலைகள் இன்றி, வாடிக்கையாளர்களின் ஷாப்பிங் அனுபவத்தை மேம்படுத்தவும், விற்பனையை அதிகரிக்கவும் இது உதவும் என்று தெரிவிக்கப்பட்டுள்ளது.

title: ID Finance Secures EUR 545 Million from International Investors
summary:
ID Finance, a leading fintech group operating in Spain and Mexico, has announced EUR 545 million of debt and equity funding with participation from international investors Spice Expeditions, WashU, Kingsway Capital and global investment firm i80 Group, who provided asset-based financing. The funding will support further growth for Plazo, ID Finance’s flagship consumer finance app and a central pillar of the company’s long-term strategy.
This transaction is one of the largest closed by a Spanish fintech in recent years and comes two years after the $150 million debt financing round provided by i80 Group in early 2024, that was utilised to grow Plazo’s credit portfolio. The round follows a year of strong financial performance for ID Finance. In 2025, the Group reported €243 million in revenue, while profit nearly doubled in the same period. Plazo achieved bottom line profitability in 2025 as its revenue grew 300% y-o-y, growing client base to over 400,000 users. This milestone validated the business model, and the new funding is now being deployed to build on this strong foundation for growth.
Together with additional financing, Plazo is expected to grow another 300% in 2026, supported by AI-powered technology infrastructure. This highlights Plazo’s rapid adoption among users and its increasing strategic importance for the Group.
As part of its continued expansion, ID Finance recently launched Turrón by Plazo, a flexible payment solution that enables customers to make online and in-store purchases. Turrón combines an e-money account, debit card and Buy Now, Pay Later (BNPL) solution. Following the launch of Turrón, the company is now focused on expanding its network of partner merchants. The addition of BNPL services marks another step towards in creating Spain’s “go-to” consumer credit platform.
Alexander Dunaev, co-founder of ID Finance said: "This investment is a strong vote of confidence in Plazo and in the model we've built to modernise consumer credit in Spain. Plazo tripled its portfolio in 2025 and reached profitability, proving that responsible, AI-driven underwriting and a genuinely better product experience can scale together. This new capital from some of the most reputable global investors in fintech lets us build on that foundation, expand Plazo's product suite and keep pushing on innovation, including through Turrón".
Tamir Saeed, Managing Partner at Kingsway Capital: “It has been a pleasure to partner with ID Finance over the last few years, supporting their mission to provide access to financial services to all consumers in Spain and Mexico. We are pleased to continue investing in this exciting next phase of ID Finance’s journey, exemplified by the high growth and disruptive potential of new products like Plazo and Turron.”
Peter Frank, Managing Director at i80, commented:
“ID Finance has done a tremendous job of managing risk while growing the portfolio. We're delighted to deepen our relationship and increase the scale of the asset-based financing that will support Plazo's next phase of growth as it continues to modernise consumer credit in Europe."

content_ta: ID Finance நிறுவனம் Spice Expeditions, WashU, Kingsway Capital மற்றும் i80 Group உள்ளிட்ட சர்வதேச முதலீட்டாளர்களிடமிருந்து 545 மில்லியன் யூரோக்கள் நிதி திரட்டியுள்ளது. இந்த முதலீடு, நிறுவனத்தின் முக்கிய செயலியான Plazo-வின் வளர்ச்சிக்கும், அதன் புதிய கட்டண சேவையான Turrón-ஐ விரிவுபடுத்துவதற்கும் பயன்படுத்தப்பட உள்ளது. Spain மற்றும் Mexico நாடுகளில் சிறப்பான நிதிச் செயல்பாடுகளைப் பதிவு செய்துள்ள இந்நிறுவனம், தனது AI தொழில்நுட்ப அடிப்படையிலான கடன் வழங்கும் சேவைகளை மேலும் பலப்படுத்த திட்டமிட்டுள்ளது.
